text:
Alex W: quick heads-up — several customers (payments + search) pinged about integrating 3rd-party tools via our function-calling surface. request: adapters that map external tool schemas to our call/result shape so they can keep existing infra.
Marta P: +1, saw this in CS backlog. Main asks: adapter SDK, explicit schema mapping rules, and clear migration path for future schema changes.
Samir K: do we mean a pluggable adapter layer server-side, or client-side translation libs? both have different tradeoffs.
Alex W: leaning server-side for hosted because it keeps routing + telemetry consistent, but customers asked for a light client lib for Private too.
Li Z: server-side adapters mean we own security model for external calls — needs RBAC + vetting. client libs push responsibility to customer.
Marta P: launch criteria suggestion: 1) adapter SDK + 2 sample adapters (slack-like, payment-proxy) 2) telemetry for adapter calls 3) clear schema versioning doc 4) fallback policy when adapter fails.
Samir K: rough cost: eng-platform ~3 sprints to wire adapter runtime + sandbox + policy controls. eng-ml needs 1 sprint to extend our schema validator.
Alex W: question: how opinionated is the adapter contract? Minimal: input JSON + metadata (caller, model, route) -> call result JSON with status + output. We can increment later.
Li Z: propose contract v1:

request: {"tool_id": "string", "payload": {...}, "meta": {"call_id":"uuid","user_id":"..."}}
response: {"status":"ok|error","result": {...}, "diagnostics": {"lat_ms": 123}}

Keep it intentionally thin.
Marta P: love thin v1. Important: include a canonical errors list so caller code can decide fast-fail vs retry.
Samir K: operationally we also need circuit-breaker + per-adapter rate limits. ops-bot should auto-disable adapters that error >X% in Y minutes.
ops-bot: noted — can wire an alert playbook: adapter_errors_high -> pause adapter -> notify #eng-oncall + #product.
Alex W: migration plan: adapters register supported schema versions. when we bump call/result envelope, adapters must declare compatible versions. if incompatible, route to fallback model variant.
Li Z: telemetry: token counts, adapter latency, adapter success rate, tool output size, and sample anonymized outputs for QA and regtests.
Marta P: for launch we should provide an "adapter test harness" customers can run locally to validate mapping without pushing to production.
Samir K: question on security: do adapters get access to keys for external services? if server-side, yes — needs KMS and scoped creds per-customer.
Alex W: for MVP -> built-in adapters can be maintained by us (hosted) with creds in KMS; for private -> provide adapter templates + docs.
Marta P: acceptance criteria checklist draft: 1) SDK + sample adapters, 2) runtime + rate limits, 3) telemetry dashboard, 4) error handling doc + tests, 5) migration/version registry, 6) security review for hosted adapters.
Li Z: prioritize telemetry + error handling first; makes rollout safe.
Samir K: agree. schedule proposal: sprint 1 = schema + SDK + sample adapters; sprint 2 = runtime + rate limits + ops automation; sprint 3 = telemetry dashboards + docs + private templates.
Alex W: customer comms: include migration guidelines and recommended retry semantics. flag for legal on data flow for hosted adapters.
Marta P: i'll slot this into roadmap and open a feature brief. can someone volunteer to draft the schema spec doc?
Li Z: i'll take the initial spec draft — will post PR by EOD tomorrow with examples and error enums.
Samir K: i'll sync with eng-platform on runtime design and start a spike for adapter sandbox.
Alex W: perfect — next sync Fri 11am. thanks all :thumbsup:
